newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Environmentalists to press BHP mining.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Environmentalists to press BHP mining.

text.p: Environmentalists plan to urge shareholders of Australia's largest company, the Broken Hill Proprietary Co Ltd, on Tuesday to reject copper and gold mine exploration in the Caribbean nation of Dominica.

Representatives from Aid Watch, the Uniting Church of Australia and National Conservation Council of New South Wales plan to address board members at BHP's annual meeting, being held here later on Tuesday, Danny Kennedy, a coordinator for the Project Underground environmental umbrella group told Reuters.

Meanwhile, BHP is expected to face criticism from shareholders at the meeting, due to start at 0430 GMT, over its 23 percent fall in first quarter profits recorded last week and its high exposure to depressed international copper markets.

The copper market collapsed in June -- about six months after BHP completed its US$2.4 billion takeover of Magma Copper Co of the U.S. -- after Japanese trading firm Sumitomo Corp revealed at least US$1.8 billion in copper trading losses.
The Magma acquisition made BHP the world's second largest copper company, producing around one million tonnes a year.
But since the Magma purchase, copper prices have fallen by about 25 US cents a pound to under 90 cents.
Each one US cent rise would add A$16 million to BHP's bottom line.
Magma operated at a loss in the latest quarter and was working on ways to reduce costs, BHP's managing director, John Prescott said last week
A BHP spokesman said any plans to actually construct a mine in Dominica are a long way off.
The company so far had only applied for exploration permits from the government, the spokesman said
In the meantime, it was consulting with all concerned stakeholders, which includes local environmental interests, over any future exploration, he said.
"You can't do much without a license," the spokesman said.

BHP recently agreed to help fund about A$110 million compensation to villagers and pick up over A$7 million in legal fees for Papua New Guinea affected by pollution of river systems from its 52 percent-owned Ok Tedi copper mine.
Kennedy said representatives at the annual meeting would try to convince shareholders that Dominica could face similar environmental problems from mining.-- Sydney 61-2 9373-1800
